findings.note: 0.8 s is not a root of this quadratic. The roots are t = (−8 ± √(64 + 36))/10 = (−8 ± 10)/10, that is t = 0.2 s and t = −1.8 s. Substituting t = 0.8 gives 5(0.64) + 6.4 − 1.8 = 7.8, not 0. The step's own why_this_step names the other root as −1.8 s, which pairs with +0.2 s (sum −1.6, product −0.36), not with +0.8 s — the solution contradicts itself on this line.

The correct crossing time is 0.2 s, printed as option 4. Starting the downward crossing at 8 m/s and falling 1.8 m under g = 10 m/s² gives 1.8 = 8t + 5t², whose positive root is 0.2 s; the speed reached at the window's bottom is then 8 + 10(0.2) = 10 m/s, which matches √(8² + 2·10·1.8) = 10 m/s. 0.8 s is the time to rise to the top of the flight (u/g), not the window-crossing time.

notes: Solved blind before opening the solution: with the origin at the window's top and up positive, the stone returns to that level at 8 m/s downward, then −1.8 = −8t − 5t² gives t = 0.2 s (option 4). The approach and steps 0 and 1 are correct — 2u/g = 1.6 s for the return to the top, and 1.8 = 8t + ½·10·t² is the right equation for the crossing — the defect is only the solved root, which then propagates into final_answer. Both common_mistakes routes were recomputed and reach the options they name: 2u/g = 1.6 s is option 2, and the bottom speed √(64 + 36) = 10 m/s divided by g gives 1.0 s, option 3. Neither condemns a correct method.
